articles.title: Perianal fistulizing Crohn's disease: emerging biology, therapeutics, and roadmap for precision treatment.
articles.abstract: Perianal fistulizing Crohn's disease (PFCD) remains difficult to treat despite integrated medical and surgical management, and no validated biomarkers are currently available to guide pharmacological treatment selection. Recent single-cell, spatial, and multiomic studies have identified immune, stromal, epithelial, and microbial features across fistula tissue and rectal mucosa, expanding the biological characterization of PFCD. In this review, we examine how these molecular advances refine the biological understanding of PFCD and inform the evaluation of current and emerging pharmacological strategies. We critically assess the efficacy, safety, and strength of clinical evidence across distinct therapeutic approaches. We also discuss how molecular insights could support biomarker development for patient stratification and treatment selection, alongside anatomical phenotype, surgical context, and standardized multidimensional assessment of fistula healing.

articles.title: Prospects for adiponectin-based therapeutics in myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract: Adiponectin is an adipocyte-derived hormone with broad cardiometabolic benefits, circulating at high levels in healthy individuals but reduced in obesity, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease. Low adiponectin concentrations are strongly associated with coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction, myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI), and heart failure. MIRI remains a major unmet need in contemporary ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) care. Although reperfusion is essential in limiting ischemic myocardial necrosis, it causes deleterious effects such as impaired carbohydrate oxidation, excessive fatty-acid oxidation, intracellular acidosis, calcium (Ca2+) overload, oxidative/nitrative stress, and mitochondrial fragmentation, that expand infarct size, worsen microvascular obstruction, and fuel adverse ventricular remodeling. Activation of the adiponectin-adiponectin receptor (AdipoR) axis directly counteracts these processes by stimulating adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-dependent metabolic rebalancing, restoring mitochondrial fusion-fission homeostasis, enhancing oxidative capacity, reducing inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS-) and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH) oxidase-mediated injury, improving endothelial nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability, and enhancing microvascular perfusion. In animal models, adiponectin or its mimetics consistently reduced infarct size, improved myocardial function, and attenuated apoptosis, inflammation, and no-reflow. A growing array of therapeutic strategies has emerged, each bringing its own pharmacologic nuances and implications for translation to the clinic. This review summarizes current strategies to enhance adiponectin action, highlights the progress in peptide and small-molecule mimetics, and discusses future directions for clinical translation in cardiometabolic diseases.

articles.title: Engineering whole tumor cell vaccines for cancer immunotherapy: From malignant cells to therapeutic vaccines.
articles.abstract: Tumor cells are the driving force of cancer progression, yet they also constitute a rich reservoir of tumor-associated and patient-specific antigens that can be harnessed for therapeutic vaccination. Whole tumor cell vaccines (WTCVs) exploit this unique duality by converting malignant cells into immunotherapeutic agents capable of eliciting broad antitumor immunity and overcoming tumor heterogeneity. However, their clinical translation remains constrained by the need to eliminate tumorigenic potential while preserving or enhancing immunogenicity. Here, we provide a comprehensive overview of recent advances in the engineering of WTCVs from the perspectives of safety assurance and therapeutic enhancement. We summarize current strategies for controlling tumorigenicity, including physical, chemical, engineered, and viability-preserving approaches, and discuss emerging immunopotentiation strategies that enhance antigen abundance and exposure, improve antigen presentation, activate innate and adaptive immune pathways, and integrate complementary therapeutic modalities. Collectively, these advances are transforming malignant cells into multifunctional therapeutic vaccines capable of eliciting potent and durable antitumor immunity. Finally, we discuss the key challenges and future opportunities for next-generation WTCVs and highlight design principles that may accelerate their clinical translation.

articles.title: Advancements in peptidomimetics as a strategy against multidrug resistance: Fundamentals, rational design, resistance mechanisms, and artificial intelligence.
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial peptides offer rapid, often membrane centered activity, but their therapeutic translation is limited by proteolytic instability, toxicity, reduced activity under physiological conditions, unfavourable pharmacokinetics, and manufacturing challenges. Peptidomimetics seek to retain the functional logic of antimicrobial peptides while improving these properties. This review presents a unified framework for peptidomimetic based antimicrobial discovery. It describes the fundamentals and classes of antimicrobial peptidomimetics, discusses mechanisms of antibacterial activity and the molecular basis of multidrug resistance. The review also highlights advances in molecular modelling and the growing role of artificial intelligence. A literature search was performed using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar to review experimental, computational, and translational studies on peptidomimetics. Relevant studies were selected. The review examines the fundamentals of peptidomimetics, including key classes, structural modifications, and optimization strategies designed to overcome antimicrobial resistance. The review also highlights that effective antibacterial action involves electrostatic accumulation, selective membrane anchoring, transition into a membrane active conformation, and, in some cases, permeation to intracellular targets. In Gram-negative organisms, lipopolysaccharide organization and Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ mediated cross linking increases the energetic barrier to membrane engagement. Furthermore, advances in synthetic methodologies, coupled with AI, are expected to enable faster and more efficient synthesis routes. Peptidomimetics seek to redefine antibacterial strategy by encoding resistance resilience into molecular design rather than relying on single target novelty. Their future impact will depend on integrating structure-activity relationships, mechanistic understanding with AI guided design.

articles.title: Saponin extract from Astragalus membranaceus (Fisch.) Bunge regulates gut-brain axis through intestinal Escherichia coli to reduce cerebral oxidative stress to treat vascular dementia in rodents.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Vascular dementia (VD) is a cognitive dysfunction syndrome caused by cerebrovascular diseases. Astragalus membranaceus (Fisch.) Bunge (AS) has antioxidative, gut microbiota-regulating, and cognitive-improving effects. Escherichia coli (E. coli) abundance is associated with cognitive dysfunction. This study explored the mechanism by which AS improves VD by regulating E. coli along the gut-brain axis, providing a basis for VD drug research and development. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: VD models were established by permanent ligation of the common carotid artery. Morris water maze, Doppler cerebral blood flow measurement, blood lipid assays, pathological staining, Western blot, and ELISA were used to evaluate AS's protective effects on the brain. 16S rRNA sequencing analyzed gut microbiota to screen differential strains. Metabolomics screened endogenous differential metabolites. Oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) was established to evaluate 5-aminovaleric acid effects on neuronal mitochondrial function and oxidative stress. KEY RESULTS: AS significantly improved cognitive dysfunction, restored cerebral blood flow, and attenuated abnormal protein accumulation and oxidative stress in VD rat brains. Microbiota analysis revealed that AS inhibited E. coli proliferation and mitigated associated pathological damage. Furthermore, endogenous metabolite 5-aminovaleric acid alleviated OGD-induced neuronal damage and oxidative stress. CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS: AS can treat cognitive dysfunction and brain injury in rodents, regulate gut microbiota balance, and reduce the contribution of E. coli. Meanwhile, AS-regulated endogenous metabolite 5-aminovaleric acid can also treat OGD-induced nerve cell injury. These findings suggest that AS may be a promising candidate for VD treatment and provide mechanistic insight into gut-brain axis regulation.

articles.title: Proteomic Profiling of Xenobiotic and Nutrient Transporters in Human Placenta of Different Gestational Ages.
articles.abstract: The placenta serves a critical role in nutrient uptake and waste elimination for the developing fetus. The placenta is also responsible for the uptake and/or exchange of xenobiotics, including medications, between the maternal and fetal bloodstreams. An estimated 40-80% of women take medications or drugs during pregnancy. Very little is understood about fetal drug and nutrient exposure during pregnancy and how it may change over the course of fetal development. This study aimed to characterize the abundance of transport proteins in placental tissue, which are important in modulating fetal nutrient and drug exposure, over the duration of pregnancy. Using a mass spectrometry-based global proteomic approach, the relative abundance of proteins in placental tissue samples was profiled from first trimester, second trimester, and term placenta samples. Our analysis detected a total of 6331 proteins which included a total of 139 solute carrier and ATP-binding cassette transport proteins that were detected across the dataset, and 80 that were quantified in every sample. In general, membrane-associated proteins, including solute carrier and ATP-binding cassette transport proteins, were significantly enriched in placental tissue collected during early gestation compared to term placental tissue. Overall, this study presents a comprehensive profiling of membrane-associated proteomic changes during gestation and identifies significant gestational age associated abundance changes at the protein level in several transport protein families. These data provide critical information to support future studies into the understanding of fetal exposure to xenobiotics and nutrients circulating in the maternal bloodstream.

articles.title: PFAS:VDR interactions and immunotoxicity through disruption of monocyte differentiation.
articles.abstract: Accumulating evidence indicates that per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have the capacity to modulate vitamin D receptor (VDR) signaling however, the underlying mechanisms governing these interactions remain poorly understood. In the present study, we investigated direct interactions between PFAS and VDR signaling, as well as a novel, putative mechanism by which PFAS may induce immunotoxicity through disruption of VDR molecular functionalities. VDR is widely expressed across both the innate and adaptive branches of the immune system, where it plays critical roles in regulating immune cell activation, differentiation, and function. While PFAS exposure has been consistently associated with immune dysregulation and reduced vaccine responsiveness in both human and animal studies, the molecular basis of PFAS-induced immunotoxicity is only partially defined. To address these knowledge gaps, we examined a panel of PFAS compounds previously identified through computational modeling to possess measurable binding affinities for the VDR. We employed a suite of complementary, orthogonal bioassays to characterize the functional interactions between PFAS and the vitamin D receptor. These included a transient transactivation assay to assess global receptor agonist and antagonist activity, a Mammalian two-Hybrid (M2H) assay to evaluate PFAS effects on VDR interactions with its obligate heterodimerization partner (RXR), coactivator (SRC-1), and corepressor (NCoR1), and a THP-1 cell differentiation/transcription assay to probe the transcriptional consequences of PFAS exposure on vitamin D-facilitated monocyte cell differentiation. Collectively, our findings reveal that select PFAS engage in complex molecular interactions with the VDR and act as potent antagonists, effectively inhibiting vitamin D-mediated receptor function and downstream THP-1 cell signaling.

articles.title: Longitudinal Proteomics Integrated with Multi‑Omics Reveal Molecular Drivers of Responses to Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Rectal Cancer.
articles.abstract: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is the standard treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC), yet its molecular determinants of response remain unclear. We conducted longitudinal 4D-DIA proteomic profiling of pre- and post-treatment specimens from 156 patients, including 31 patients with matched pre- and post-treatment specimens, and integrated with bulk RNA sequencing, single-cell transcriptomics, and functional validation. At baseline, responders were enriched in innate and adaptive immune pathways, whereas non-responders showed proliferative and metabolic programs. Pre-treatment RAC2, elevated in responders, was positively associated with immune activation, oxaliplatin sensitivity, and survival, and was validated in GSE139255 and GSE35640 (all P < 0.05). Moreover, RAC2 demonstrated strong predictive performance (training AUC = 0.867; testing AUC = 0.857). During treatment, NAC induced fibrosis-related remodeling across all groups (all P < 0.05), while responders uniquely preserved CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration (P = 0.031). Responders and RAC2-high tumors exhibited concordant pathway dynamics during NAC. Single-cell analysis further revealed that pre-treatment tumor RAC2, higher in responders, transmitted signals to CD8⁺ T cells while receiving inputs from fibroblasts (P < 0.05). In vitro and in vivo, RAC2 knockdown reduced baseline tumor growth but promoted under oxaliplatin (all P < 0.05). Overall, this study offers proteomic insights into NAC in LARC, supports therapeutic decision-making, and identifies potential targets.

articles.title: AI-Guided Identification of a Covalent SMAD3 Regulatory Mechanism of Celastrol in Diabetic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Renal fibrosis is a defining pathological feature of diabetic kidney disease (DKD) and a major contributor to progressive renal dysfunction. Although aberrant activation of transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)/SMAD3 signaling is a central driver of renal fibrogenesis, effective targeted therapies remain limited. Here, using an AI-guided target-prioritization strategy based on the deep learning platform Uni-Mol, we selected Celastrol for experimental investigation and subsequently characterized its molecular interaction with SMAD3. Activity-based protein profiling combined with a competitive iodoacetamide-based probe assay identified SMAD3 as a direct covalent target of Celastrol, which was further supported by molecular docking and site-directed mutagenesis. Mechanistically, Celastrol preferentially engages the non-phosphorylated form of SMAD3 and promotes KPNB1-dependent nuclear translocation, resulting in the premature nuclear accumulation of functionally inactive SMAD3 and reduced association of SMAD3 with TGFBR1. In parallel, Celastrol disrupts the interaction between SMAD3 and SMAD4, thereby limiting the formation of transcriptionally active SMAD complexes and attenuating profibrotic signaling. Collectively, our findings identify SMAD3 Cys421 as a functionally relevant covalent site for Celastrol engagement and reveal a previously uncharacterized mechanism by which Celastrol regulates the spatial and functional state of SMAD3. These findings provide mechanistic insight into the antifibrotic activity of Celastrol and may inform the future development and optimization of Celastrol-based therapeutic strategies for renal fibrosis in DKD.

articles.title: Pharmacological TRPM8 blockade reprograms patient-derived intestinal fibroblasts and mitigates experimental fibrosis through modulation of myofibroblast activation.
articles.abstract: Intestinal fibrosis is a major long-term complication mostly prevalent in Crohn's disease (CD) and remains without approved antifibrotic therapies. Transient receptor potential melastatin 8 (TRPM8) is a pharmacologically targetable ion channel involved in inflammatory regulation, but its contribution to intestinal fibrotic remodeling is unknown. This study investigated TRPM8 association with human stenotic CD and whether pharmacological TRPM8 modulation limits fibroblast activation and experimental intestinal fibrosis. TRPM8 expression was increased in stenotic ileocolonic tissues from CD patients and in primary patient-derived intestinal fibroblasts. In these cells, the TRPM8 antagonist AMTB reduced proliferation and migration at non-cytotoxic concentration and attenuated the expression of fibroblast activation, matrix and myofibroblast-associated markers. In mice with chronic 2,4,6-trinitrobenzenesulfonic acid (TNBS)-induced intestinal fibrosis, AMTB reduced disease activity and endoscopic severity and attenuated stromal remodeling-associated gene expression. Histological analyses further showed reduced tissue injury and collagen remodeling, supported by Masson's Trichrome staining and quantitative analysis of Picrosirius Red. In contrast, pharmacological TRPM8 activation with WS12 did not significantly modify fibroblast proliferation in vitro or the evaluated clinical, endoscopic and molecular readouts in vivo. AMTB also reduced the TNBS-induced T helper 17 response without reducing interleukin-23 production by colonic mononuclear phagocytes. Finally, fibroblasts isolated from AMTB-treated fibrotic mice displayed reduced expansion, lower collagenogenic gene expression, reduced contractile/activated fibroblast markers and decreased actin cytoskeletal remodeling ex vivo. Overall, these findings identify TRPM8 as a druggable regulator of fibroblast-driven intestinal remodeling and support TRPM8 antagonism as a candidate antifibrotic strategy for stricturing CD.

articles.title: SRSF1-DLAT axis drives mitochondrial fusion to confer therapy resistance in diabetes-associated pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and concurrent diabetes mellitus frequently exhibit poor outcomes. This study aims to elucidate the molecular mechanism linking diabetes with therapeutic failure. METHODS: We integrated clinical analysis, diabetic-KPC mouse models, multi-omics approaches including scRNA-seq and eCLIP-seq analysis, and functional validations to investigate the mechanisms of therapy resistance in PDAC associated with diabetes. RESULTS: It was found that pancreatic cancer with concurrent diabetes is prone to chemoresistance, which is accompanied by Serine/arginine-rich splicing factor 1(SRSF1)-driven altered splicing and expression of Dihydrolipoamide S-Acetyltransferase(DLAT). Our results showed that lactate accumulation in the diabetic tumor microenvironment induces K48-lactylation and stabilization of SRSF1. Crucially, stabilized SRSF1 directly binds to DLAT pre-mRNA, promoting the retention of Exon 5. This enhanced exon retention prevents nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) of DLAT, thereby elevating DLAT protein levels.The resulting SRSF1/DLAT axis drives mitochondrial hyperfusion, conferring chemoresistance by inhibiting senescence and apoptosis. Furthermore, the hyperfusion of mitochondria facilitates immune evasion by promoting the acetylation and stabilization of PD-L1. Notably, pharmacological intervention with Berberine effectively suppressed this SRSF1-DLAT axis, thereby re-sensitizing diabetes-associated PDAC tumors to combined chemo- and immunotherapy in vivo. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings reveal that the SRSF1-DLAT-mitochondrial fusion axis drives therapeutic resistance in diabetes-associated PDAC. Targeting this metabolic-immune crosstalk offers a promising strategy for PDAC treatment.

articles.title: Antidepressant effects of artemisinin and its derivatives: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled animal studies.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Depression imposes a substantial global disease burden. Current pharmacotherapies are often limited by a delayed onset of action, significant adverse effects, and high costs. Preclinical studies have indicated that artemisinin and its derivatives possess neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory properties and have demonstrated antidepressant-like effects in rodent models. However, no meta-analysis has yet been performed on these preclinical rodent studies. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the antidepressant efficacy of artemisinin in rodent models of depression-like behavior and to identify potential factors influencing the variability in treatment effects. METHODS: This study systematically searched four databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure), including randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published up to May 2026. All data were statistically analyzed using a random-effects model, yielding standardized mean differences (SMDs) with their 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Subgroup analyses were conducted based on rodent species, depression-like modeling methods, intervention timing, duration, and frequency. Publication bias was assessed using Egger's test, funnel plots, and trim-and-fill analyses. Sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate result robustness. The risk of bias was evaluated using the Systematic Review Centre for Laboratory Animal Experimentation (SYRCLE) tool, and the overall certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. RESULTS: A total of 17 studies involving 402 rodents were included in the analysis. Compared with the control group, artemisinin reduced immobility in the TST and FST, increased sucrose preference in the SPT, alleviated anxiety-like behaviors in the OFT and EPM, and improved cognitive performance in the MWM, Y-maze, and NOR. Subgroup analyses identified intervention duration, frequency, species, modeling methods, and derivative type as impactful moderators. Sensitivity tests validated stable outcomes. While Egger's test hinted at publication bias in the OFT, TST, and FST datasets, trim-and-fill analyses imputed zero missing studies, although this does not fully exclude publication bias given the limited number of studies. Under the GRADE framework, the certainty of evidence was rated as very low for most outcomes due to high risk of bias, substantial heterogeneity, and indirectness. DISCUSSION: Artemisinin can ameliorate depression-like and anxiety-like behaviors and improve cognitive function. These findings provide a basis for further investigation into artemisinin as an adjunctive therapeutic agent for depression. However, the certainty of evidence is very low due to methodological limitations in the included preclinical studies, and additional clinical trials are required to evaluate its efficacy in humans.

articles.title: One protein, many faces: TRAF1 from signaling hub to disease diversity.
articles.abstract: Tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 1 (TRAF1) is a unique member of the TRAF family, distinguished by its lack of an N-terminal RING domain. At the transcriptional level, TRAF1 expression is regulated by diverse mechanisms, including methylation, RNA-binding domain (RBD) proteins, and microRNAs. Post-translationally, TRAF1 undergoes modifications such as M1-linked ubiquitination and phosphorylation. In immune signaling pathways, TRAF1 usually displays functional duality: it activates the canonical NF-κB pathway by enhancing cIAP recruitment downstream of TNFR1, whereas at death domain-lacking TNFR superfamily members (NDDTNFRs), it drives the non-canonical NF-κB pathway through TRAF3 degradation. Conversely, TRAF1 often acts as a negative regulator in Toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling. Within the MAPK pathway, TRAF1 participates in modulating multiple cascades, including ASK1/B-Raf(BRAF)/ERK1. In immune-mediated diseases, TRAF1 contributes to disease pathogenesis by regulating inflammatory cytokines, matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) expression, synovial cell apoptosis and tissue destruction. In infectious diseases, the anti-apoptotic effect of TRAF1 downstream of the 4-1BB signaling pathway serves as a host strategy to combat viral infections by preserving CD8+ T cell survival. However, Helicobacter pylori exploits TRAF1 upregulation to inhibit apoptosis in gastric epithelial cells, facilitating its persistent colonization. This contrast highlights TRAF1's functional diversity across infections. This review summarizes the post-translational regulation of TRAF1, its dual roles in signaling pathways, and its contributions to immune-related and infectious diseases, aiming to clarify its mechanistic complexity within the existing biological framework.

articles.title: Vepdegestrant (ARV-471): pharmacokinetics, drug metabolism and clinical translation of an oral ERα-targeting PROTAC.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Vepdegestrant (VEPPANU) is an orally administered proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC) that targets estrogen receptor-α (ERα), a main transcription regulator of estrogen receptor-positive (ER+)/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2-) breast cancer. AREAS COVERED: The molecule consists of a lasofoxifene-based ER-binding part and a rigid, nitrogen-containing linker with a glutarimide-based CRBN (cereblon)-binding part related to lenalidomide. Preclinical studies show extensive degradation of both wild-type and mutant ERα, while clinical pharmacology studies demonstrate clinically relevant oral exposure despite the molecule's beyond-Rule-of-5 (bRo5) physicochemical properties. The review integrates the absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion of vepdegestrant with its event-driven pharmacology, CYP3A4-, P-glycoprotein- and BCRP (Breast Cancer Resistance Protein)-mediated drug-drug interactions, and the translational implications of oral PROTAC design. The literature was identified through a search of Scopus from database inception through 31 August 2026, supplemented by screening of relevant reference lists and appropriate regulatory and clinical-trial information. EXPERT OPINION: Vepdegestrant is a paradigm shift in the field of targeted protein degradation in endocrine oncology, yet its huge molecular size, metabolic problems, drug-drug interactions, development of resistance and persistent toxicological profile are all relevant matters of concern.

articles.title: Interpreting variability in atypical antipsychotic levels: a practical review for TDM.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) is a valuable tool for optimizing antipsychotic pharmacotherapy, especially in the context of interindividual variability in drug metabolism, adherence assessment, and treatment resistance. AREA COVERED: Factors affecting TDM include genetic polymorphisms, age, sex, smoking status, drug-drug interactions, comorbidities (e.g. hepatic or renal impairment, obesity, and inflammation), physiological variations, and adherence. The pharmacokinetic parameters of antipsychotics and the role of active metabolites are important for accurately interpreting of TDM results. The metabolites norclozapine, paliperidone, dehydroaripiprazole, and didesmethyl-cariprazine contribute to the therapeutic effect. Norquetiapine has antidepressant effects, but also has strong anticholinergic adverse effects. The parent-to-metabolite ratio can serve as a marker of metabolic capacity, adherence patterns, and potential drug interactions. EXPERT OPINION: Genotype-guided prescribing is expected to integrate more closely with TDM, using genetic information to select antipsychotics and estimate initial dosing while TDM reveals the patient's current functional metabolic phenotype shaped by adherence, inflammation, smoking, organ dysfunction, diet, and concomitant medications. The concept of phenoconversion can modify metabolic activity independently of genotype, making combined genotype-plus-phenotype assessment essential for individualized antipsychotic therapy. Future psychiatric TDM will increasingly integrate pharmacogenetics, pharmacokinetic modeling, and Bayesian forecasting.

articles.title: Drug repurposing in fibrosis: From molecular networks to antifibrotic therapeutics-A narrative review.
articles.abstract: Fibrosis is a common pathological endpoint of chronic diseases affecting multiple organs and remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite advances in understanding fibrogenesis, current antifibrotic therapies primarily slow rather than reverse disease progression, underscoring the need for more effective treatments. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy by leveraging the established safety and pharmacokinetic profiles of approved drugs while reducing development time and cost. This review provides a mechanism-based synthesis of repurposed agents targeting the interconnected pathways driving fibrosis, including transforming growth factor-β signalling, chronic inflammation, oxidative stress and emerging regulatory networks such as mechanotransduction and cellular senescence. Evidence from mechanistic studies, preclinical models, randomized trials and meta-analyses is critically appraised, highlighting promising candidates and translational challenges arising from the distinct cellular mechanisms and variable reversibility of fibrosis across organs. By integrating molecular insights with clinical evidence, this review advocates a pathway-guided, biomarker-driven approach to drug repurposing as a rational strategy for accelerating development of personalized, multi-target antifibrotic therapies.

articles.title: Hybutimibe, an innovative cholesterol absorption inhibitor for lipid-lowering therapy: current evidence and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: Achievement of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) targets is crucial for the prevention of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). As first-line lipid-lowering drugs, statins often fail to achieve adequate LDL-C control rates in clinical practice due to individual variations in efficacy, safety concerns, and poor long-term adherence. Cholesterol absorption inhibition mediated by the Niemann-Pick C1-like 1 (NPC1L1) pathway provides a complementary approach to statin-based lipid lowering regimens. Hybutimibe is an oral NPC1L1 inhibitor approved in China and has reported pharmacokinetic characteristics that differ from those of ezetimibe; however, the clinical relevance of these differences has not been established in direct comparative studies. Evidence from Phase I-III clinical trials and post-marketing real-world studies indicates that hybutimibe monotherapy or combination therapy with statins can achieve significant and sustained LDL-C reduction; in patients with inadequate response to statin monotherapy, combination with hybutimibe exhibits superior lipid-lowering efficacy compared to statin dose escalation, with favorable overall safety. However, available studies have primarily evaluated LDL-C and other lipid parameters as surrogate endpoints. No dedicated cardiovascular outcome trial has established whether hybutimibe reduces major adverse cardiovascular events, cardiovascular mortality, or all-cause mortality. This article systematically reviews the research and development background, pharmacological properties, mechanism of action, clinical efficacy, safety, and post-marketing real-world evidence of hybutimibe, exploring its application value as an adjuvant therapy in optimizing clinical LDL-C management.

articles.title: Unsaturated fatty acids as immunometabolic modulators in high-risk pregnancies: mechanisms, clinical evidence, and translational perspectives.
articles.abstract: High-risk pregnancies (HRPs) are characterized by the convergence of metabolic dysfunction, chronic low-grade inflammation, and placental maladaptation, leading to increased maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. Emerging evidence indicates that these conditions are driven by a tightly integrated immunometabolic axis, in which metabolic stress activates innate immune pathways, amplifying systemic and placental inflammation. Unsaturated fatty acids (UFAs), including monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), have gained attention as key modulators of this axis. Omega-3 PUFAs, such as eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), influence membrane composition, lipid mediator synthesis, and intracellular signaling pathways involved in inflammation and metabolism. At the cellular level, these fatty acids attenuate pro-inflammatory signaling through nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB), modulate inflammasome activation, improve mitochondrial function, and promote the production of specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs), thereby facilitating the resolution of inflammation. Clinical evidence from observational studies, randomized controlled trials, and meta-analyses supports the role for omega-3 supplementation in reducing the risk of preterm birth, particularly among women with low baseline DHA status. However, findings for other outcomes, including preeclampsia and gestational diabetes, remain heterogeneous, likely reflecting variability in study design, baseline nutritional status, dosage, and timing of intervention. Although several studies support a beneficial role of omega-3 supplementation, the overall clinical evidence remains heterogeneous. While reductions in preterm birth are consistently observed, findings for other outcomes, such as preeclampsia and gestational diabetes, are inconsistent across randomized controlled trials. Differences in study design, baseline nutritional status, timing, dosage, and adherence likely contribute to these discrepancies. Importantly, several well-conducted trials have reported null effects, highlighting the need for cautious interpretation and more targeted approaches. This review synthesizes current evidence on the immunometabolic mechanisms underlying HRPs and highlights UFAs as biologically plausible and clinically relevant modulators. It focuses on the importance of precision nutrition approaches that incorporate baseline nutritional assessment and biomarker-guided stratification which may ultimately improve maternal and fetal outcomes in high-risk populations.

articles.title: Cellular memory after cancer therapy: persistence after drug withdrawal, maintenance across cell divisions, and responses to rechallenge.
articles.abstract: A fraction of tumor cells can survive therapy without acquiring stable resistance mutations and enter a drug-tolerant persister (DTP) state. After drug withdrawal, these cells may resume proliferation and regain drug sensitivity, retain phenotypic features that alter survival or death upon retreatment, or continue to evolve toward stable resistance. The DTP designation describes survival under therapeutic pressure but does not establish whether the associated state persists after treatment ends. The term post-treatment cellular memory is used here operationally for a treatment-associated state that remains detectable after adequate drug washout and can influence a later response. Evidence can be evaluated across three experimental dimensions: persistence after withdrawal, maintenance across subsequent cell divisions or clonal descendants, and a functional consequence upon re-exposure. These dimensions indicate different strengths of support rather than mandatory diagnostic criteria. The review therefore organizes representative studies by what was measured after withdrawal rather than by DTP markers or mechanisms alone. Recent work indicates that AP-1 can contribute to encoding treatment-associated transcriptional states and that CBP/p300 activity can help maintain an established reporter state, including after drug withdrawal; however, molecular persistence does not substitute for demonstrating altered function upon rechallenge with the original agent. Chromatin remodeling, transcriptional state transitions, antioxidant metabolism, autophagy, organelle homeostasis, and lineage plasticity may prolong residual-cell survival. Their biological consequences differ: some states decay after withdrawal, some create time-limited vulnerabilities to ferroptosis or to therapeutic targeting of anti-apoptotic dependencies, and others extend the interval during which genetic resistance can emerge. Lineage tracing, single-cell multi-omics, withdrawal-rechallenge experiments, and longitudinal sampling of minimal residual disease can help distinguish transient stress responses from persistent post-treatment states. These observations provide a rationale for testing whether treatment sequence and interventions during residual disease can be matched to the reversibility and vulnerabilities of residual states.

articles.title: Advances and challenges in inner ear drug delivery: limitations and therapeutic perspectives.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Hearing loss is a major global health burden, with age-related hearing loss affecting hundreds of millions of people worldwide. Despite significant therapeutic advances, effective treatment remains hampered by the challenge of delivering drugs to the inner ear, an anatomically inaccessible and tightly protected organ. AREAS COVERED: This narrative review was based on an extensive search of major biomedical databases and focuses on the anatomical and physiological barriers that limit inner ear drug delivery, current and emerging administration routes, and advanced delivery systems, including hydrogels, nanoparticles, microdevices and implantable platforms. Particular attention is given to the factors governing nanocarrier performance and to the key challenges for clinical translation, such as species-dependent pharmacokinetics, manufacturing reproducibility, GMP-compatible scale-up and regulatory requirements. Studies published between 2001 and 2026 were identified through PubMed, Embase, Web of Science and ClinicalTrials.gov. EXPERT OPINION: Despite rapid preclinical innovation, clinical translation remains uneven. Systemic sodium thiosulfate provides the strongest regulatory proof of clinically meaningful otoprotection, whereas recent intracochlear gene therapy establishes an important benchmark for localized treatment. For nanomedicine, progress will depend less on platform novelty than on rational structure-property design, reproducible cochlear exposure, cell-resolved biodistribution, large-animal validation, GMP-compatible manufacturing, patient stratification and clinical trial design.

articles.title: Impurities of impurities! Investigation of drug-related nitrosated impurities of omeprazole using optimized forced nitrosation conditions.
articles.abstract: Omeprazole (OMP) is-one of the most commonly prescribed proton pump inhibitors for treating acidity, heartburn, and gastric/duodenal ulcers. The present work investigates nitrosation susceptibility of OMP to form drug-related nitroso impurities using optimized protocols employing forced nitrosation workflow in alignment with nitrosation assay procedure (NAP) and modified NAP. This approach allows evaluation of nitrosation propensity of OMP as well as its degradation products. A series of 10 distinct N-nitrosation products (NPs) were successfully identified and separated via gradient elution liquid chromatography on a C18 stationary phase (250 mm × 4.6 mm, 5 µm) using 10 mM ammonium acetate and acetonitrile as mobile phases. Chemical structures of all the NPs were characterized using LC-QTOF-MS/MS analysis. The in-silico toxicity predictions indicated carcinogenic and mutagenic potential of the observed N-nitrosated impurities alongside qualitative risks such as hepatotoxicity, immunotoxicity, and respiratory toxicity in several cases. These findings underscore elevated risks from nitroso-impurities of API degradation products, beyond conventional API-focused assessments, urging expanded monitoring in pharmaceutical manufacturing and stability studies to minimize the patient exposure and enhance consumer safety.

articles.title: Population pharmacokinetics of levetiracetam in term neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and therapeutic hypothermia: The LEVNEONAT-1 study.
articles.abstract: AIM: This study aimed to describe the pharmacokinetics (PK) of levetiracetam (LEV) in term neonates treated for neonatal seizures secondary to hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE). METHODS: Fifteen neonates were included and received a loading dose ranging from 30 to 60 mg/kg followed by eight maintenance doses corresponding to one-fourth of the loading dose every 8 h. Five blood PK samples were drawn for each neonate: three after the loading dose and two after the last maintenance dose. Data were analysed by a population approach using NONMEM software. The possible relationship between LEV Cmax and AUC from time 0 to 4 h after the loading dose (AUC4h) and the relative seizure difference (RSD) that defined the LEV efficacy was investigated by linear regression. RESULTS: LEV PK was described by a two-compartment model with allometric scaling based on body weight. Typical values (%IIV) for LEV CL, central and peripheral distribution volume (Vc and Vp) and distribution clearance (Q) were 4.27 (15%) L/h, 46.5 (14%) L, 6.10 L (98%) and 1.75 L/h, respectively. Creatinine clearance (CLcr) and natremia were found to be significant covariates for LEV clearance (CL), CL increasing with CLcr and natremia. No relationship was found between LEV Cmax or AUC4h and RSD. CONCLUSION: A population PK model of LEV in term neonates with HIE was developed. The influence of natremia was highlighted for the first time and could reflect the relationship between the encephalopathy severity and LEV PK in this population.

articles.title: Yupingfeng alleviates allergic rhinitis by modulating gut microbiota and succinate to inhibit mTOR/S6K signaling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Yupingfeng granules (YPF), derived from the classic traditional Chinese medicine prescription Yupingfeng powder, have been recommended in clinical practice guidelines for the management of allergic rhinitis (AR), and their clinical efficacy is widely recognized. However, the underlying pharmacological mechanisms have not been thoroughly investigated. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate whether YPF protects the nasal epithelial barrier and alleviates AR by modulating the gut microbiota and pathways related to its metabolites. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An OVA-induced AR mouse model was established and phenotypically evaluated. The dependence of YPF efficacy on gut microbiota was assessed by 16S rRNA sequencing, antibiotic depletion, and fecal microbiota transplantation. 1H-NMR metabolomics was used to identify key metabolites, followed by exogenous supplementation for validation. Nasal mucosal transcriptome sequencing was performed to explore downstream pathways, and functional validation was conducted in OVA-induced HNEpCs through metabolite intervention, YPF co-treatment, mTOR knockdown, and MHY1485 treatment. RESULTS: YPF dose-dependently reduced nasal rubbing and sneezing, attenuated IgE-mediated type 2 inflammation, and ameliorated nasal epithelial barrier injury in OVA-induced AR mice. YPF remodeled the gut microbiota and increased microbial diversity. Gut microbiota depletion attenuated the protective effects of YPF, whereas FMT from YPF donors reproduced them. Metabolomic analysis identified succinate as a key YPF-responsive metabolite, and exogenous succinate aggravated nasal epithelial barrier injury. Transcriptomic analysis suggested that succinate-induced nasal mucosal injury may involve mTOR signaling activation. In vitro, succinate aggravated OVA-induced barrier injury in HNEpCs, with disrupted Occludin distribution and enhanced mTOR/S6K phosphorylation, whereas YPF co-treatment reversed these changes. mTOR knockdown mimicked the protective effects of YPF, whereas MHY1485 attenuated them. CONCLUSION: YPF alleviates OVA-induced AR by remodeling the gut microbiota, reducing succinate accumulation, and suppressing mTOR/S6K signaling to preserve nasal epithelial barrier integrity.

articles.title: Integrative Target Fishing and Proteomics Reveal the Molecular Targets of Abrus cantoniensis in Alleviating Dyslipidemia.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Abrus cantoniensis (AC) is a traditional Chinese medicinal herb used for hepatitis, with demonstrated lipid-regulating activity. However, as a multi-component herbal system, the specific bioactive monomers and their direct protein targets remain to be elucidated. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study integrates target fishing with proteomics to capture hepatic protein targets of AC and elucidate its lipid-regulating mechanisms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Abrine, a pharmacopoeial marker compound employed as a probe, was used to synthesize abrine-functionalized magnetic beads (Fe3O4-SH-BP-abrine, FSBA) via photo-crosslinking for target capture from mouse liver lysates. Proteins were identified by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Bioinformatic analyses, including Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG), were conducted. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), immunohistochemistry (IHC), and Western blotting (WB) were employed for validation. RESULTS: AC ameliorated hepatic steatosis in HFD-induced dyslipidemic mice. KEGG enrichment identified the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) as the top-ranked pathway, consistent with its central role in NADPH-dependent lipid biosynthesis. Molecular docking and MD simulations predicted stable interactions between abrine and PPP enzymes. SPR verified a direct interaction between abrine and G6PD. RT-qPCR demonstrated downregulation of G6pd, Tkt, Taldo1, H6pd, and Aldoa at the mRNA level. IHC and WB consistently showed reduced protein expression of G6PD, PGD, and TKT after AC treatment. CONCLUSIONS: Target fishing combined with proteomics uncovered AC's anti-dyslipidemic mechanism via the PPP. The identified PPP-related targets provide mechanistic insight into AC's lipid-regulating activity.

articles.title: Carum carvi L. alleviates skin depigmentation by suppressing STAT1-mediated inflammatory responses.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Vitiligo is an acquired depigmenting disorder characterized by CD8+ T cell-mediated melanocyte destruction. While JAK inhibitors exhibit efficacy, their clinical application is limited by adverse effects, high costs, and pediatric contraindications. Carum carvi L. (CCL), an esteemed medicinal plant in traditional Uyghur and Tibetan medicine, is frequently prescribed to treat refractory skin diseases, notably vitiligo. AIM OF THE STUDY: We aimed to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of CCL against vitiligo, elucidate its underlying pharmacological mechanisms, and identify its potential active monomer. METHODS AND MATERIALS: A monobenzone-induced vitiligo mouse model was utilized to assess macroscopic, histological, and molecular recovery following oral administration of the CCL. To elucidate the pharmacological mechanisms and identify key bioactive constituents, we integrated RNA-seq, UPLC-Orbitrap-MS/MS chemical profiling, network pharmacology, serum constituent screening, and molecular docking. The identified candidate monomer was subsequently validated through B16F10 cell assays, and an in vivo murine model. RESULTS: In vivo, both the CCL and Rob restored repigmentation, restoring melanin deposition and functional follicular melanocytes. In vitro and in vivo experiments confirmed that Rob inhibited STAT1 activation and attenuated the downstream CXCL9/10 chemokine cascade. This targeted modulation reduced localized inflammation, characterized by decreased macrophage infiltration and a phenotypic shift toward pro-repair (CD206+) macrophages, and restricted CD8+ T cell recruitment. CONCLUSIONS: CCL and its active monomer Rob effectively mitigates immune-mediated melanocyte destruction and promotes repigmentation. Rob drives targeted therapeutic intervention by suppressing the STAT1-macrophage-CD8+ T cell inflammatory axis. These findings suggest CCL as a promising, multi-targeted natural therapy for vitiligo.

articles.title: Radiolabelled cyclodextrins to detect cervical cancer: a preclinical feasibility study.
articles.abstract: Radiolabelled cyclodextrins targeting prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) seem promising candidates for positron emission tomography (PET)-based molecular imaging of cervical cancer. Here, we evaluated the performance of gallium-68-labelled 2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HPβCD) and randomly methylated β-cyclodextrin (RAMEB) for the in vivo PET detection of cervical cancer. P-glycoprotein positive (Pgp+) KB-V-1 and P-glycoprotein negative (Pgp-) KB-3-1 cervical carcinoma xenografts of varying sizes (small-, medium-, large-sized) were established and subjected to [68Ga]Ga-NODAGA-HPβCD and [68Ga]Ga-DOTAGA-RAMEB PET imaging followed by ex vivo biodistribution and immunohistochemical (IHC) analysis of PGE2 and Pgp expression. In line with the IHC results, PET data revealed the capability of both radiotracers to reliably detect each tumor types independent of tumor size. Nevertheless, the modest increase in uptake observed with increasing size may indicate enhanced tumor aggressiveness and angiogenic activity. Comparable radiotracer accumulation in MDR-positive and MDR-negative tumors suggests that HPβCD and RAMEB derivatives are unlikely to serve as substrates of Pgp enabling tumor detection across different tumor types. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that radiolabelled cyclodextrins are promising PET tracers for the in vivo detection of cervical cancer, irrespective of tumor size and Pgp expression.

articles.title: Apatinib attenuates CRKII-Mediated angiogenesis: Possible implications for metastasis prevention from small extracellular vesicle proteomics.
articles.abstract: High postoperative recurrence severely compromises treatment for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) surgical outcomes. We investigated Apatinib's potential as an adjuvant therapy targeting sEV (Small Extracellular Vesicle)-mediated angiogenesis within the tumor microenvironment to identify novel prognostic biomarkers. We employed quantitative label-free proteomics to screen for key therapeutic targets in TNBC-derived sEVs. The anti-angiogenic efficacy and potential anti-metastatic activityof Apatinib was evaluated using in vitro functional assays (proliferation, migration, adhesion, invasion, and tube formation) and an in vivo TNBC syngeneic mouse model. To validate its translational potential, we analyzed the regulation of the CRKII-PXN/VEGFA axis and its correlation with tumor angiogenesis and growth inhibition. Proteomic analysis identified the adaptor protein CRKII as a central hub significantly downregulated by Apatinib in sEVs. Mechanistically, Apatinib disrupted the transmission of pro-angiogenic signals to endothelial cells by reducing sEV-CRKII (small extracelluar vesicle-CRKII), which subsequently inhibited the downstream CRKII-PXN/VEGFA signaling axis. Functional validation confirmed that CRKII knockdown mimicked, while overexpression reversed, the anti-angiogenic effects of Apatinib. In the preclinical model, Apatinib significantly suppressed tumor growth and reduced microvessel density, suggesting its efficacy in controlling tumor burden and potential micrometastases. Apatinib effectively inhibits TNBC angiogenesis and exhibits potential anti-metastatic activity by downregulating sEV-CRKII and blocking the CRKII-PXN/VEGFA axis. These findings suggest that Apatinib may have potential as a postoperative adjuvant therapy for metastasis prevention. Furthermore, sEV-CRKII emerges as a promising non-invasive biomarker for surgeons to monitor therapeutic response and recurrence risk in TNBC patients.

articles.title: Characterization of F-30 as an FGFR2/4-selective covalent inhibitor with activity against clinically relevant mutations.
articles.abstract: Fibroblast growth factor receptors FGFR2 and FGFR4 are oncogenic drivers in multiple cancers, yet most approved FGFR inhibitors lack subtype selectivity and are prone to acquired resistance. Here we identify F-30 as, to our knowledge, the first covalent inhibitor with preferential activity toward both FGFR2 and FGFR4 through covalent targeting of a conserved P-loop cysteine. Structural analyses reveal that differential engagement of the P-loop and surrounding binding environment contributes to paralog discrimination. Consistent with these structural observations, F-30 showed an approximately 12-fold lower KI and 13-fold higher kinact/KI for FGFR2 than for FGFR1, whereas their kinact values were comparable. These results indicate that the preference for FGFR2 over FGFR1 is primarily established during pre-covalent recognition. F-30 retained strong activity against multiple clinically relevant FGFR2 resistance-associated mutations but showed reduced potency against gatekeeper mutations. In cellular models, F-30 preferentially inhibited the proliferation of FGFR2/4-driven cancer cells, while substantially weaker pathway inhibition was observed in FGFR1- and FGFR3-driven models than in FGFR2-dependent cells. Taken together, these findings identify structural and kinetic features that contribute to the subtype-selective profile of F-30 and may guide the design of covalent FGFR inhibitors targeting the conserved P-loop cysteine.

articles.title: Comparison of alveolar macrophages senescence between cigarette smoke-exposed and naturally aged mice and the role of P2X7R in CS-induced airway inflammation.
articles.abstract: Aging is intricately linked to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Alveolar macrophages (AMs) senescence-induced impaired phagocytosis may contribute to persistent airway inflammation in COPD. The P2X7 receptor (P2X7R) is a crucial modulator of cellular senescence. However, its roles in AMs senescence and phagocytosis remain unclear. In this study, naturally aged mice, cigarette smoke (CS)-exposed mice, and MH-S cells stimulated by cigarette smoke extract (CSE) were used to compare the degree of AMs senescence and phagocytosis between CS-exposed and naturally aged mice, and to confirm the function and mechanism of P2X7R. Results showed that pulmonary function gradually declined, AMs senescence increased, and phagocytosis decreased with increasing age. CS-exposed mice exhibited similar levels of AMs senescence and impaired phagocytosis as aged mice, but more severe pulmonary dysfunction, histopathological damage, and airway inflammation. P2X7R was elevated in AMs from CS-exposed mice and CSE-treated MH-S cells. Mechanistically, the P2X7R antagonist A438079 reduced ROS levels and p-p38 MAPK, restored SIRT1 expression, and reduced Ac-NF-κB p65, thereby alleviating cellular senescence and impaired phagocytosis in CSE-treated MH-S cells. Tert-butyl hydroperoxide, a ROS inducer, can reverse the protective effects of A438079. In vivo, treatment with A438079 alleviates AMs senescence and impaired phagocytosis, and improves pulmonary dysfunction, histopathological damage, and airway inflammation in CS-exposed mice. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that the degree of AMs senescence and impaired phagocytosis is similar between CS-exposed and aged mice. Furthermore, CS may induce AMs senescence and impaired phagocytosis via the P2X7R-mediated ROS/p38 MAPK/SIRT1/NF-κB pathway, thereby driving airway inflammation.

articles.title: CFD-DEM simulation of capsule vibration facilitated powder discharge and dispersion in Breezhaler.
articles.abstract: This study presents a computational fluid dynamics-discrete element method (CFD-DEM) investigation on drug discharge and dispersion processes driven by capsule rotation and capsule-device collisions in Ultibro® Breezhaler®, where a layering dynamic mesh method is employed to characterize the capsule's complex rotational and vibrational motions, and a multi-scale model is adopted to evaluate the powder dispersion performance by predicting the fine particle fraction (FPF) based on carrier particle-wall collisions. The capsule vibration, either in continuous or intermittent regime, is found to effectively shake cohesive particles off the capsule wall, break particle clusters, and promote uniform particle distribution, facilitating complete drug discharge. Whereas, neglecting capsule vibration significantly underestimates the actual drug discharge efficiency. The particles inside the capsule and the rotation chamber are subjected to the strongest mechanical contact forces and aerodynamic forces with the former at least one order of magnitude greater than the latter. The capsule vibration is found to enhance both types of forces, particularly within the capsule. More importantly, capsule vibrations significantly increase the total number of particle-particle and particle-wall collisions in the inhaler, boosting the overall collision intensity relative to the none capsule vibration case. The predicted FPFemitted values for cases incorporating either continuous or intermittent capsule vibration regimes show good agreement with the experimental data, while the value for the none capsule vibration case is markedly lower. This highlights the necessity of incorporating the capsule vibration into the CFD-DEM model and validates the applicability of multi-scale model for predicting powder dispersion performance in the Breezhaler®.

articles.title: Mechanisms underlying the promotion of intestinal absorption of baohuoside I by Dipsacus asperoides saponin fractions and their synergistic anti‑osteoporosis efficacy in combination.
articles.abstract: Baohuoside I (BA) is the key active ingredient in the compound anti-osteoporosis preparation Xianlinggubao; however, its poor solubility and permeability result in low oral bioavailability. This study systematically investigated, from both pharmaceutical and pharmacological perspectives, the role of Dipsacus asperoides saponins fractions (DAS) in enhancing BA absorption and their synergistic anti-osteoporosis effects. From a pharmaceutical perspective, DAS significantly improves BA's solubility, membrane permeability, and gastrointestinal stability, and forms nanocomposites with BA through noncovalent interactions (as verified by DSC, TEM, FT-IR, and molecular dynamics simulations). In vivo intestinal perfusion experiments in rats confirmed that DAS enhances BA absorption in all intestinal segments; in a Caco-2 monolayer cell model, DAS inhibited MRP2/BCRP efflux and reversibly opened tight junctions, increasing the apparent permeability coefficient of BA from (1.62 ± 0.21) × 10⁻⁶ to (4.25 ± 0.45) × 10⁻⁶ cm/s; Oral pharmacokinetic studies in rats further confirmed that the AUC0-∞ was significantly higher in the BA-DAS combination group. Pharmacologically, in an ovariectomized mouse model, the combination of BA and DAS significantly improved bone microstructure and serum bone metabolism markers compared to BA alone. Urinary non-targeted metabolomics results further revealed that this synergistic effect is associated with the regulation of Ascorbate and aldarate metabolism, Glycine, serine, and threonine metabolism, and Tryptophan metabolism pathways. In summary, DAS promotes BA absorption through a dual mechanism of inhibiting efflux and opening tight junctions, and the combination of BA and DAS produces a synergistic anti-osteoporotic effect, providing a mechanistic explanation for the formulation of traditional Chinese medicine.

articles.title: Trehalose-modulated poloxamer 407 thermosensitive hydrogel: sol-gel transition regulation and sustained low-dose pilocarpine nitrate delivery.
articles.abstract: Traditional ophthalmic solutions and viscous gels are limited by insufficient precorneal residence time, inaccurate dosing administration, and inconvenient sterile filtration. Pilocarpine, originally a classic muscarinic acetylcholine receptor agonist for glaucoma management, has been recently repurposed for presbyopia treatment; however, its clinical application is greatly restricted by frequent severe ocular adverse reactions, including xerophthalmia and conjunctival hyperemia. Herein, trehalose was adopted to modify poloxamer 407 thermosensitive hydrogel, on the basis of its dual functions of tuning gel physicochemical properties and enhancing cellular desiccation resistance. The incorporation of trehalose lowered the critical gelation threshold concentration of poloxamer 407 without impairing the intrinsic physicochemical properties of the hydrogel. The optimized formulation exists as a low-viscosity aqueous solution (approximately 50 mPa·s) at ambient temperature, which allows convenient sterilization via 0.22 μm filtration, and rapidly undergoes in-situ sol-gel transition on the ocular surface to form isotonic hydrogel. This hydrogel protects loaded pilocarpine against hydrolytic degradation and improves corneal hydration. In vivo rabbit ocular irritation tests verified that the formulation effectively alleviates pilocarpine-induced ocular irritation. Benefiting from excellent thermal stability and industrial processability, this delivery system exhibits promising translational prospects and lays a solid foundation for follow-up clinical research on presbyopia treatment.

articles.title: Preoperative sleep deprivation prolongs postoperative hyperalgesia by downregulating spinal cord D2R expression via the PP2A/AKT-dependent NMDA receptor phosphorylation.
articles.abstract: Preoperative sleep deprivation (SD) is known to exacerbate postoperative pain, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Using a male mouse model of 48-hour continuous SD followed by incisional surgery, we found that SD alone induced transient mechanical hyperalgesia, and when combined with surgery (SI group) it significantly aggravated and prolonged postoperative pain recovery until day 10. On postoperative day 7, SI mice showed marked downregulation of spinal dopamine D2 receptor (D2R) expression and decreased spinal dopamine concentration. D2R was predominantly expressed on spinal glutamatergic neurons. Overexpression of D2R on these neurons via intrathecal AAV injection effectively alleviated the prolonged hyperalgesia, normalizing pain sensitivity by day 7. Mechanistically, D2R downregulation led to increased phosphorylation of NMDA receptor subunits (p-NR1 and p-NR2B) without altering total NMDA receptor levels. Co-immunoprecipitation revealed an interaction between D2R and protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A). SI mice exhibited decreased PP2A expression but increased p-AKT, p-GSK3β, and β-catenin, indicating activation of the PP2A/AKT signaling pathway, which were reversed by D2R overexpression. Furthermore, pharmacological activation of PP2A with DT-061 not only downregulated p-AKT, p-GSK3β, β-catenin, p-NR1 and p-NR2B, but also produced significant analgesia in SI mice. Collectively, these results demonstrate that preoperative sleep deprivation prolongs postoperative hyperalgesia by downregulating spinal D2R on glutamatergic neurons, which disinhibits the PP2A/AKT pathway and enhances NMDA receptor phosphorylation. Targeting D2R or its downstream PP2A/AKT signaling may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for managing persistent postoperative pain caused by preoperative sleep deprivation in male mice.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic interaction of enavogliflozin, a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, with glimepiride and metformin in healthy participants.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Enavogliflozin, a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, is expected to be coadministered with antihyperglycaemic drugs with different mechanisms of action. This study aimed to investigate the pharmacokinetic (PK) and pharmacodynamic (PD) interactions between enavogliflozin, glimepiride and metformin. METHODS: A randomized, open-label, two-sequence, three-period crossover study was conducted. Participants received one of the following three treatments for 6 days in each period: enavogliflozin 0.3 mg once daily (E), glimepiride 2 mg once daily and metformin 1000 mg twice daily combination (GM) or the combination of all three study drugs (E + GM). Serial blood and urine samples were collected for PK and PD assessments at steady state. RESULTS: The geometric mean ratios (GMRs) and 90% confidence intervals (CIs) for the maximum plasma concentration (Cmax,ss) of enavogliflozin, glimepiride and metformin were 1.0811 (1.0273-1.1378), 1.1495 (1.0602-1.2464) and 1.0556 (0.9937-1.1215), respectively. The corresponding values for the area under the plasma concentration-time curve within a dosing interval (AUCτ,ss) were 1.0031 (0.9541-1.0545), 1.2264 (1.1383-1.3213) and 1.1638 (1.0958-1.2361) respectively. A 24-h urinary glucose excretion (UGE0-24h) induced by E was affected by coadministration of GM, with the GMR (90% CI) of 0.7834 (0.7307-0.8400). Serum glucose reduction was greatest with the E + GM, followed by GM, and then E. CONCLUSIONS: No clinically meaningful PK interaction of enavogliflozin, glimepiride and metformin was observed. Although a reduction in UGE0-24h was observed, an additive PD interaction was observed in serum glucose levels. The results suggest that enavogliflozin can be coadministered with glimepiride and metformin without requiring dose adjustments of either of these drugs.

articles.title: Integrated serum pharmacochemistry , network pharmacology, untargeted metabolomics and experimental validation to explore the mechanism of Wenjian Qigong Decoction in the treatment of polycystic ovary syndrome.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), a prevalent endocrine and metabolic disorder among women of reproductive age, currently has no definitive treatment. Qigong Wan (QGW), first documented in Yifang Jijie, is a classic prescription for infertility in obese women. Given the heterogeneous and complex nature of PCOS, Wenjian Qigong Decoction (WJQG), a modified formula derived from QGW that incorporates medicinal ingredients from Jiawei Buzhong Yiqi Decoction (JWBZYQ), Guishen Wan (GSW), and Jiaotai Wan (JTW), exhibits remarkable therapeutic efficacy for obese PCOS in clinical practice. The efficacy of all constituent herbs in WJQG has been confirmed, whereas its pharmacological mechanisms remain to be clarified. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the potential therapeutic benefits of WJQG for the treatment of PCOS and provide mechanistic insights into its mode of action. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An obese PCOS rat model was established via testosterone propionate (TP) injection combined with a 45% high-fat diet (HFD). The therapeutic efficacy of WJQG, as well as the validity of the model, was evaluated by assessing body weight, visceral fat content, estrous cycle, clinical chemistry indicators, and histopathology. Furthermore, a comprehensive approach integrating ovarian untargeted metabolomics, serum pharmacochemistry , network pharmacology, molecular docking, and experimental validation was employed to systematically elucidate the potential mechanism of action of WJQG in treating obese PCOS. RESULTS: WJQG significantly attenuated body weight gain, reduced abdominal visceral fat, restored estrous cyclicity, improved ovarian morphology, and corrected hyperandrogenemia and endocrine dysregulation in obese PCOS rats. Serum pharmacochemistry identified 22 bioactive prototype compounds absorbed into the blood. Network pharmacology predicted hub targets including TNF, IL6, CASP3, and PTGS2. Subsequent molecular docking simulations indicated favorable binding affinities between these proteins and representative prototype constituents such as narirutin, ginsenoside Rc, and hyperoside. Untargeted metabolomics suggested that WJQG substantially remodeled the ovarian metabolome, specifically suppressing the hyperactivated arachidonic acid metabolism pathway and downregulating downstream pro-inflammatory lipid mediators (PGF2α, PGA2, PGE2, and 10,11-dihydro-20-hydroxy-LTB4). Mechanistically, WJQG inhibited the enzymatic cascade of p-cPLA2, COX-2 (encoded by PTGS2), and 5-LOX. Meanwhile, WJQG treatment was associated with restored ADPN/PPARα/p-AMPK signaling, a predominance of M2-type macrophages, a suppressed NLRP3/NF-κB inflammatory cascade accompanied by reduced TNF-α and IL-6 levels, and alleviated granulosa-cell apoptosis alongside decreased caspase-3 activation. CONCLUSIONS: WJQG alleviates key disease manifestations in obese PCOS rats, which correlates with modulation of the interconnected pathological triad of intra-ovarian arachidonic acid metabolism hyperactivation, chronic inflammation, and granulosa-cell apoptosis. These findings provide supportive scientific evidence and pharmacodynamic rationale to support further pre-clinical investigation of WJQG as a potential integrative therapeutic candidate for PCOS.

articles.title: Crosstalk through cholinergic and aryl hydrocarbon receptor pathways in the anti-inflammatory actions of microbial metabolites.
articles.abstract: The intestinal epithelium maintains immune and metabolic homeostasis at the host-microbiota interface, and its disruption contributes to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Microbial metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and indole derivatives are known to regulate epithelial and immune functions, but their roles in cholinergic signaling and aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) pathways remain incompletely understood. Caco-2 intestinal epithelial cells were stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS; 10 µg/mL) and co-treated with SCFAs (acetate, propionate, butyrate) or indole derivatives (IAA, IPA, IBA; 1000 µM). The AhR antagonist CH223191 was used to assess receptor involvement. Inflammatory markers (TNF-α, IL-6, COX-2), barrier integrity (FITC-dextran permeability, ZO-1 and occludin), cholinergic components (CHAT, ACHE, BCHE, α7nAChR, mAChR1, mAChR3), and AhR activation (nuclear localization, CYP1A1 expression) were analyzed using qPCR, ELISA, immunostaining, and enzymatic assays. Molecular docking was performed to predict metabolite-protein interactions. LPS induced inflammatory cytokine expression and barrier disruption, whereas SCFAs and indole derivatives significantly reduced inflammation, restored tight-junction organization, and decreased permeability. These metabolites enhanced CHAT and muscarinic receptor expression while suppressing ACHE upregulation, indicating restoration of cholinergic balance. Both groups reactivated AhR signaling, and AhR inhibition disrupted cholinergic regulation, supporting an AhR-dependent mechanism. Butyrate and indole-3-butyric acid exhibited the strongest protective effects. These findings identify a novel AhR-cholinergic axis in intestinal epithelial regulation and highlight microbial metabolites as promising therapeutic candidates for IBD.

articles.title: Anti-inflammatory versus metabolic therapy in MASLD: a randomized clinical trial of aspirin and dapagliflozin using fibroscan outcomes.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a major hepatic consequence of metabolic dysfunction, yet evidence-based pharmacologic options remain limited. Repurposing widely available agents with metabolic and anti-inflammatory actions may offer a clinically meaningful benefit. To compare the effects of aspirin and dapagliflozin on hepatic steatosis, fibrosis, liver enzymes, and lipid profile in patients with MASLD. In this prospective randomized interventional study, 80 adults with confirmed MASLD were allocated (1:1) to aspirin 100 mg once daily or dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily for 6 months (n = 40 per group). Baseline and 6-month measurements included alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), triglycerides, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), total cholesterol, and FibroScan-derived parameters, including controlled attenuation parameter (CAP; dB/m), which quantifies hepatic steatosis, and liver stiffness measurement (LSM; kPa), a surrogate marker of liver fibrosis. The primary endpoints included the between-group differences in changes in LSM, CAP, liver enzymes, and lipid profile from baseline to 6 months. Ethics approval was obtained (FMBSUREC/04032025). The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07338331) on 20 Dec 2025. Dapagliflozin significantly improved hepatic steatosis, reflected by lower CAP values compared to aspirin (260.35 ± 20.78 vs 271.48 ± 12.58 dB/m; p = 0.005), and reduced total cholesterol levels (138.87 ± 54.70 vs 192.48 ± 79.46 mg/dL; p = 0.003). In contrast, aspirin demonstrated a greater reduction in liver stiffness (LSM) (6.15 ± 2.55 vs 8.58 ± 4.13 kPa; p = 0.002) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) percentage change (- 44.54% vs - 17.84%; p = 0.025). Other biochemical parameters showed no statistically significant between-group differences (all p > 0.05). Aspirin and dapagliflozin exert distinct and potentially complementary effects in MASLD, with dapagliflozin preferentially improving hepatic steatosis and aspirin showing a greater impact on fibrosis-related parameters. These findings support a dual-pathway therapeutic model targeting steatosis and fibrosis and underscore the need for larger trials evaluating combined strategies and histological outcomes.

articles.title: Systematic qualitative analysis of the designation of medicinal products in the Rote Liste® (Red List).
articles.abstract: Medication errors are a serious problem in medicine and can lead to patient harm and entail high costs. To investigate the quality of brand names which we suggest can favor medication errors, this study looks at the designation of drugs (brand name). It analyses whether they are potentially a risk for medication errors by presenting a false image of the drug. The Rote Liste® (Red List) is one of the best-known drug directories in Germany; this drug directory was used for the categorization of medicinal products. The entries included in the Rote Liste ® dataset from 2020 were analyzed by their semantic appearance. By creating a new methodology, the entries were examined for an association between the designation of the medicinal product and their attributes, such as the RL-group, the active ingredients and the marketing authorization holder, and were divided into three main categories. Subsequently, correlations between the results of the analysis and the attributes were performed. To verify the quality of this method, the inter- and intra-rater-reliability was determined by using Cohen's cappa. One thousand six hundred thirty-seven (22.36%) of the entries had a strictly generic designation. Three main categories were established, of which most entries (5454; 74.49%) were assigned to the category "coherent". The other two categories are "incoherent" (1625; 22.19%) and "potentially confusing" (243; 3.32%). By looking at the distribution of the three main categories among the RL-groups, a few RL-groups condition for the most entries in the category "potentially confusing". The inter- and intra-rater-reliability for this newly established analysis shows a moderate to substantial agreement. The results show that there are heterogenous linguistic forms of designation of medicinal products. A more transparent and uniform designation of medicinal products could lead to a reduction in medical errors. In this paper, we have provided specific suggestions on how drug naming could be improved.

articles.title: Panax ginseng suppresses endothelin-1-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy through inhibition of the local angiotensin II-AT1 receptor signaling axis.
articles.abstract: Panax ginseng (PG) is a traditional herbal medicine widely used for the treatment of cardiovascular disorders in East Asia. Although PG has been reported to attenuate cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, the molecular mechanisms underlying its cardioprotective effects remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated whether modulation of the endothelin-1 (ET-1)-angiotensin II (AngII) signaling axis contributes to the anti-hypertrophic action of PG. Neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs) were used to evaluate ET-1-induced hypertrophy, and pharmacological experiments using receptor antagonists were performed to examine the signaling pathways involved. Extracellular AngII levels were quantified by ELISA, intracellular Ca2+ accumulation was assessed in AT1AR-overexpressing NRVMs, and whole-cell patch-clamp recordings were performed in HEK293T cells co-expressing AT1AR and TRPC6. PG significantly attenuated ET-1-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy without altering ETAR or ETBR expression. Pharmacological experiments with the ETAR antagonist BQ-123 suggested that the anti-hypertrophic effect of PG could not be explained solely by direct inhibition of ETAR signaling. PG markedly suppressed ET-1-induced extracellular AngII production, and interaction studies with losartan further implicated the AngII-AT1AR pathway in the anti-hypertrophic action of PG. Moreover, PG inhibited AngII-induced intracellular Ca2+ accumulation in AT1AR-overexpressing NRVMs and attenuated AngII-evoked TRPC6-mediated membrane currents without affecting basal channel activity. These findings demonstrate that PG suppresses ET-1-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy by inhibiting both ET-1-induced AngII production and downstream AT1AR-dependent signaling, identifying suppression of the AngII-AT1AR signaling axis as a key mechanism underlying its cardioprotective effects.
