articles.title: Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers and the Risk of Alzheimer's Disease Progression: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: We investigated the effects of angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs) on the progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). This retrospective cohort study used data from the Korean nationwide claims data to identify patients with AD aged 60-79 years in 2010. ARB users and nonusers were 1:1 propensity score matched. Cox proportional hazards regression evaluated AD progression, defined as memantine initiation and mortality. Active-comparator and dose-response analyses were conducted. ARB use was associated with lower risks of memantine initiation (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.70-0.89) and mortality (HR = 0.83; 95% CI = 0.76-0.89). Cumulative exposure analyses showed stronger associations in the highest exposure categories, including 2-3 years of ARB use and ≥ 2 DDD-years, whereas associations in the lower exposure categories were not statistically significant. In active-comparator analyses, ARBs were associated with lower mortality risk than ACE inhibitors and beta-blockers, but not with dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (CCBs). ARB use may be a reasonable antihypertensive choice in patients with AD, although the comparable outcomes between ARBs and CCBs suggest that these associations may not be unique to ARBs and may instead reflect shared blood pressure-lowering and vascular effects. Further prospective research is warranted to optimize antihypertensive selection in patients with AD.

articles.title: Saroglitazar protects against cadmium-induced hepatorenal injury in rats by suppressing NF-κB and upregulating Nrf2.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cadmium (Cd) toxicity is one of the major public health problems because of its long half-life (10-30 years). Exposure to Cd can cause toxicity that affects several organs, including the liver and the kidney. Saroglitazar is highlighted in this study as a potential preventative medication against hepatic-renal damage induced by Cd in rats. METHODS: Cd (3 mg/kg) was injected for five successive days to induce hepatic and renal damage. Saroglitazar (2 and 4 mg/kg/day) was given orally for five successive days concurrently with Cd. RESULTS: Saroglitazar effectively improved hepatic and renal function and structure. In the meantime, saroglitazar mitigated the oxidative stress caused by Cd; it increased the level of reduced glutathione (GSH) and the activity of superoxide dismutase (SOD) and decreased malondialdehyde (MDA) content. Saroglitazar-treated groups showed a significant reduction in hepatic and renal nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB), tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, and interleukin-6 (IL-6). Furthermore, saroglitazar pretreatment significantly increased nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2); furthermore, there was a marked reduction in the expression of caspase-3 in both hepatic and renal tissues. CONCLUSION: Collectively, saroglitazar showed a protective effect against Cd-induced hepatorenal injury in rats.

articles.title: Mitochondria-targeted peptide elamipretide alleviates cisplatin-induced ovarian failure by activating the nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2/heme oxygenase-1 pathway.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Premature ovarian failure (POF) is a complex endocrine disorder that severely impairs female fertility. Cisplatin, a commonly used chemotherapeutic agent, has been identified as a major risk factor for POF in young women. This study aimed to investigate the protective effects and underlying mechanisms of the mitochondria-targeted peptide elamipretide (SS31) in a cisplatin-induced mouse model of POF. METHODS: POF was established via intraperitoneal cisplatin (2 mg/kg, 7 days), followed by SS31 treatment (10 mg/kg, 3 weeks). RESULTS: SS31 treatment significantly alleviated cisplatin-induced ovarian damage and reversed key pathological features of POF. Mice treated with SS31 exhibited more rapid recovery in body weight, increased ovarian size and weight, improved ovarian morphology, and a significantly higher number of follicles at various developmental stages compared to the model group. SS31 also normalized serum hormone levels, reduced oxidative stress, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, and improved mitochondrial morphology in oocytes and granulosa cells. Mechanistically, SS31 activated the nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2)/heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) signaling pathway in ovarian tissues. CONCLUSION: The mitochondria-targeted peptide SS31 effectively ameliorates cisplatin-induced POF in mice by enhancing antioxidant defenses and preserving mitochondrial function. These findings suggest that SS31 is a promising therapeutic candidate for the clinical management of POF and provide new insights into antioxidant-based interventions.

articles.title: Oliceridine and morphine differentially modulate the gut microbiota-intestinal barrier axis in a rat postoperative pain model.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Oliceridine is a novel G protein-biased μ-opioid receptor agonist with potentially improved gastrointestinal tolerability compared with conventional opioids. However, its impact on postoperative intestinal homeostasis-specifically the gut microbiota and intestinal barrier-remains poorly understood. METHODS: A postoperative pain model was established in male Sprague-Dawley rats using the Brennan plantar incision method. Animals were randomly assigned to four groups: non-incision control (CON), plantar incision plus normal saline, plantar incision plus oliceridine (OLI, 1 mg/kg subcutaneous bolus followed by continuous infusion at 1 mg/kg/day for 72 h), and plantar incision plus morphine (MF, 5 mg/kg subcutaneous bolus followed by continuous infusion at 5 mg/kg/day for 72 h). Analgesic efficacy was assessed by mechanical withdrawal threshold (MWT) and area under the curve (AUC). Intestinal morphology, epithelial Claudin-1 expression by immunofluorescence (n = 4 per group), gut microbiota composition (16S rRNA gene sequencing, n = 6 per group), and host ileal transcriptomic profiles (RNA-seq, n = 3 per group) were evaluated. RESULTS: Oliceridine and morphine produced comparable analgesia, as reflected by MWT AUC (P < 0.0001 vs. NS; OLI vs. MF: P = 0.8770). Both opioids alleviated postoperative mechanical hypersensitivity. Compared with NS, opioid treatment increased the relative abundance of Limosilactobacillus and Lactobacillus and decreased Streptococcus. Exploratory microbiome analysis identified a potential Lactobacillus-related signal, but no genus-level difference between the OLI and MF groups remained significant after multiple-testing correction. Transcriptomic analysis revealed distinct ileal gene-expression profiles between the OLI and MF groups. Relative to MF, OLI was associated with higher expression of genes related to epithelial barrier integrity and brush border function and lower expression of genes involved in immune-related pathways. Histologically, both opioids attenuated intestinal injury compared with NS, with no significant difference between OLI and MF. In contrast, relative Claudin-1 fluorescence intensity was significantly higher in the OLI group than in the MF group (P = 0.036), providing protein-level support for the barrier-related transcriptomic findings. Integrated correlation analysis identified associations between Lactobacillus-related taxa and host genes linked to barrier function and metabolism (|r| > 0.6, P < 0.01). CONCLUSION: Oliceridine and morphine produced comparable analgesia. Exploratory microbiome analysis identified a potential Lactobacillus-related signal, but no genus-level differences remained significant after multiple-testing correction. Oliceridine was associated with a distinct ileal transcriptomic profile and higher Claudin-1 fluorescence intensity than morphine, although histological injury did not differ between the two groups. The functional significance of these molecular differences requires further investigation.

articles.title: Silybum marianum peptide-rich fraction alleviates acute liver injury by inhibiting TRAF3/NIK/NF-κB and is associated with changes in gut microbiota composition.
articles.abstract: Acute liver injury (ALI) is a severe and prevalent condition that can progress to irreversible liver damage and failure. This study aimed to investigate the prophylactic hepatoprotective potential of Silybum marianum peptides (SMP) in ALI and elucidate its underlying mechanisms. Using a carbon tetrachloride (CCl4)-induced ALI mouse model, we evaluated the dose-dependent effects of SMP. Additionally, we explored the modulatory effects of SMP on the NF-κB pathway, gut microbiota composition, and metabolite profiles. The role of SMP in the TRAF3/NIK/NF-κB signaling axis was further validated in a NIK-overexpressing Hepa1-6 cell model. Our results demonstrated that 14-day SMP administration did not significantly affect body weight, fasting blood glucose levels, or liver and spleen weights, and no significant difference in serum ALT activity was observed. Notably, SMP (200 mg/kg) significantly alleviated CCl4-induced liver injury, as evidenced by enhanced hepatic antioxidant capacity, reduced expression of proinflammatory cytokines, and attenuated immune cell infiltration. Furthermore, SMP was associated with changes in gut microbiota composition and community structure in CCl4-induced ALI mice. Mechanistically, SMP suppressed the TRAF3/NIK/NF-κB pathway. These findings highlight SMP as a promising candidate for the prevention of CCl4-induced ALI, acting through multimodal mechanisms involving anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and gut microbiota-associated pathways.

articles.title: Liver enzyme elevations during statin-ezetimibe therapy in ABCG2 c.421C>A variant carriers: a case series and narrative review.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Statin-ezetimibe combination therapy is widely used and generally well tolerated; however, liver enzyme elevations may occur during treatment and can be difficult to interpret in patients with polypharmacy and other contributing factors. The potential role of drug-drug-gene interactions (DDGIs) in this context remains insufficiently explored. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We present a series of 11 patients from the PGx-CardioDrug study, selected for documented liver enzyme elevations during statin-ezetimibe therapy that led to treatment modification and carriage of the ABCG2 c.421A allele. Clinical characteristics, treatment history, laboratory findings, and outcomes were reviewed alongside available pharmacogenetic results for genes involved in drug transport and metabolism. Available records of five additional ABCG2 c.421CA carriers with documented normal liver enzyme findings during combination therapy were reviewed for descriptive comparison. A narrative review of the literature was conducted to provide a mechanistic interpretation for the observed findings. RESULTS: The series included six women and five men, aged 27-78 years. Muscle symptoms and/or creatine kinase (CK) elevations were observed in six patients, including two with rhabdomyolysis requiring hospitalization. Dose reduction, drug discontinuation, or switching to alternative lipid-lowering therapy resulted in improvement of laboratory parameters in several patients. In two patients, abnormalities persisted or increased during subsequent ezetimibe monotherapy. Follow-up laboratory results were not available for all patients. Eight patients had the ABCG2 c.421CA genotype and three had c.421AA, consistent with the selection criterion. Additional findings included variants in SLCO1B1, ABCC2, ABCB1, and UGT1A1. In the five potential comparators, normal liver enzyme findings during combination therapy were supported by numerical laboratory values in three patients and clinical documentation in two. DISCUSSION: These cases illustrate the difficulty of interpreting liver enzyme elevations during statin-ezetimibe therapy in patients with concomitant medications and other contributing factors. The narrative review provides a pharmacokinetic rationale for considering DDGIs, but the case series does not establish their contribution to the observed abnormalities. Genotype-based selection, incomplete clinical data, and the small descriptive comparator group limit interpretation. These observations remain hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Spica Prunellae attenuates ER stress via GRP78/IRE1α/JNK pathway in CCL4-induced acute liver injury in mice.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of Spica Prunellae (SP) on CCl4-induced acute liver injury (ALI) in mice and its regulation of the endoplasmic reticulum stress pathway. METHODS: In the toxicity test, ICR mice were administered SP decoction (2 g/kg, crude herb/mouse weight) by gavage for 10 days. Liver and kidney tissues were collected for H&E staining, and serum levels of liver function (AST, ALT) and renal (BUN, SCR) function indicators were measured. After confirming safety, 48 ICR mice were randomly assigned to normal, model, high-, medium-, and low-dose SP, and positive control groups (n = 8 per group). All mice, except the normal group, received a 10% CCl4/peanut oil intraperitoneal injection to induce ALI. The normal and model groups received saline; the positive control group received bifendate; and the SP groups received corresponding SP doses by daily gavage for 10 days. Body weight, liver, spleen, and thymus indices were recorded; ELISA measured serum ALT and AST, and liver MDA and SOD; liver histopathology was assessed by H&E staining; hepatocyte ultrastructure was examined via transmission electron microscopy; and ER stress-related proteins (GRP78, IRE1α, and JNK) expressions were determined by Western blot. RESULTS: SP caused minimal damage to hepatic and renal tissues in mice at 2 g/kg, with no significant changes in liver (ALT, AST) or renal (BUN, SCR) function indicators (p > 0.05). In the ALI model vs. model group, SP-treated groups demonstrated improved organ indices (p < 0.05), reduced serum ALT and AST levels (p < 0.05), increased SOD levels (p < 0.05), and significantly decreased MDA levels (p < 0.01). Histopathological analysis revealed clear attenuation of liver tissue damage, with mild nuclear deformation. Endoplasmic reticulum degranulation was alleviated, showing an organized arrangement and preserved cellular structure. Compared to the model group, GRP78 and IRE1α expression were significantly declined in the positive control and SP-treated groups (p < 0.01, p < 0.05), and JNK expression was downregulated (p < 0.05). CONCLUSION: These findings suggest the involvement of the GRP78/IRE1α/JNK signaling pathway in the hepatoprotective action of SP against CCl4-induced ALI.

articles.title: Retraction Note: Protective effects of hesperidin against MTX-induced hepatotoxicity in male albino rats.
Durable complete response to tislelizumab in advanced pMMR cervical cancer and successful rechallenge after immune-related NSTEMI: a case report.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have substantially improved long-term oncologic outcomes in patients with advanced malignancies; however, ICI-related cardiovascular adverse events have emerged as a growing clinical challenge. Accumulating clinical evidence confirms that ICI treatment markedly increases the risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Although cardiovascular toxicities secondary to ICIs are relatively infrequent, these complications carry severe and potentially fatal clinical consequences. Herein, we describe a rare case of acute non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) complicated by accelerated atherosclerosis potentially associated with ICI therapy in a middle-aged woman with advanced cervical squamous cell carcinoma harboring proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) status. Following successful coronary revascularization, the patient safely reinitiated immunotherapy and achieved long-term sustained tumor-free survival. CASE PRESENTATION: A 39-year-old woman was diagnosed with International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage IVB cervical squamous cell carcinoma, with comorbid type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension. She received first-line quadruple combination therapy comprising nab-paclitaxel, cisplatin, bevacizumab, and tislelizumab. Complete tumor response was achieved following six cycles of systemic treatment. Subsequent maintenance therapy combined with pelvic radiotherapy enabled sustained disease remission for more than 5 years. Approximately 2 years after transitioning to single-agent tislelizumab maintenance, the patient experienced an acute NSTEMI. Coronary angiography demonstrated severe multivessel coronary stenosis, and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) was performed successfully. After thorough multidisciplinary cardio-oncology evaluation, tislelizumab was safely reinitiated and continued until August 2024. At the most recent follow-up in June 2026, the patient maintained a persistent complete response with stable cardiac function. CONCLUSION: This case highlights that patients with advanced pMMR cervical cancer complicated by diabetes and hypertension can achieve durable complete remission exceeding 5 years with tislelizumab-based combination regimens. Furthermore, this case report also suggests that ICIs may be associated with cardiovascular events secondary to accelerated atherosclerosis, and demonstrates the clinical feasibility of safely resuming immune-checkpoint-inhibitor therapy following myocardial infarction.

articles.title: Meropenem Exposure, Target Attainment, and Therapeutic Drug Monitoring Practices in Critically Ill Adults Receiving Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To critically evaluate meropenem pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics (PK/PD) target attainment, therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM), infusion strategies, and clinical outcomes during continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). DATA SOURCES: Ovid MEDLINE, PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to August 15, 2026, using meropenem, TDM, β-lactam, and CRRT terms, with adult, human, and English-language limits. STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Thirteen reports representing 12 unique studies (2 randomized, 10 non-randomized) reporting meropenem concentration data during CRRT were included. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using RoB 2 or ROBINS-I. DATA SYNTHESIS: Total clearance ranged from 3.60 to 6.6 L/h. Lower or primary PK/PD target non-attainment ranged from 0% to 26.7%, while aggressive-target non-attainment ranged from 0% to 53.3% in most analyses and reached 93% in 1 study when a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 8 mg/L was assumed. Continuous or prolonged infusion may facilitate sustained exposure, but comparative evidence was limited. Four used routine TDM; only 2 implemented protocolized TDM-guided dose adjustment. Low exposure was associated with higher mortality in 1 adjusted observational analysis, but evidence for clinical outcomes was of very low certainty. RELEVANCE TO PATIENT CARE AND CLINICAL PRACTICE: Standardized meropenem regimens cannot be assumed to provide consistent exposure during CRRT. Optimized infusion and timely, protocolized TDM may support individualized dosing when multidisciplinary expertise is available. CONCLUSIONS: Available evidence supports a shift from standardized empirical dosing toward individualized, measurement-guided meropenem therapy in patients receiving CRRT.

articles.title: Integrating New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) into Read-Across Evidence Streams for Short-Chain Nitroparaffins.
articles.abstract: Read-across is commonly used to fill data gaps for chemical registration and safety assessment. Current read-across guidelines recommend systematic approaches for evaluating suitability of analogue data for assessing target chemical data gaps. However, these frameworks still lack practical approaches for consistently integrating diverse evidence, such as data from new approach methodologies (NAMs), into final read-across determinations. Herein, we present a case study of integration of multiple lines of evidence, including NAMs, to assess the suitability of a read-across from nitromethane (NM) to nitroethane (NE) and 1-nitroproane (1NP). The three nitroparaffins are structurally similar, which historically was considered sufficient evidence for read-across. However, data from several other lines of evidence suggest that read-across is not appropriate. The nitroparaffins differ in terms of physicochemical, toxicokinetic, toxicological, and toxicodynamic properties, as well as the identity of aldehyde metabolites. Our analysis reaffirms current guidelines that grouping chemicals based on shared functional groups alone is not a sufficient read-across justification. Further, our analysis demonstrates how NAMs can serve as a critical component to the overall evidentiary basis for read-across arguments, which will be particularly impactful in cases where extant in vivo data is insufficient to make a read-across determination with high confidence.

articles.title: Cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic acid diisononyl ester (DINCH) and its metabolites in body fluids of rats and humans after single oral doses of DINCH.
articles.abstract: The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) has established a tolerable daily intake (TDI) of 1mg/kg bw/d for the plasticizer DINCH (Cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic acid diisononyl ester). To characterize the maximum internal doses resulting from a single dosing and to assess species differences relevant for extrapolating rat toxicokinetics to humans, concentration-time profiles of DINCH and its metabolites (specific monoesters: MINCH, OH-MINCH, oxo-MINCH, cx-MINCH; non-specific metabolite: CHDA) were quantified in the blood of male Wistar rats and male human volunteers. Urinary excretion of metabolites was additionally evaluated for humans. Single oral doses of ring-deuterated DINCH were administered (rats: 1 or 40mg/kg bw; humans: 1mg/kg bw). In rats, gastrointestinal absorption exhibited saturation, as a 40-fold increase in administered dose resulted in only ~25-fold increases in Cmax and AUC. Across species, the hierarchy of Cmax in blood was consistent: DINCH > CHDA > cx-MINCH > MINCH > OH-MINCH > oxo-MINCH. Notably, Cmax values for DINCH and MINCH in blood after a 1mg/kg bw (1.74µM and 0.10µM) dose in humans were like those observed in rats following a 40-fold higher dose (4.4µM and 0.11µM). Corresponding AUC∞ values showed the same pattern, indicating greater systemic availability of DINCH in humans, although this is partly counter balanced by plasma protein binding. In humans, approximately 50% of MINCH and 70-80% of the other monoester metabolites were glucuronidated, whereas these metabolites remained unconjugated in rats. CHDA was unconjugated in both species. Overall, the data highlight both shared and species-specific features of DINCH metabolism in rats and humans.

articles.title: Evaluation of Clinical Outcomes of Selective Versus Nonselective Beta-Blockers Among Patients With Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction Receiving Sacubitril/Valsartan.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Beta-blockers, selective (metoprolol succinate or bisoprolol) and nonselective (carvedilol), and angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors (ARNIs) are the first-line guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Concomitant use of carvedilol and ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) may result in additive vasodilatory effects, which may increase the risk of hypotension and limit dose titration of sacubitril/valsartan. OBJECTIVE: This study examines differences in clinical endpoints between selective and nonselective beta-blocker therapy among patients with HFrEF receiving sacubitril/valsartan. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study utilized TriNetX Research Collaborative real-world data. Patients receiving sacubitril/valsartan concomitantly with carvedilol were identified as the intervention cohort, while those receiving metoprolol succinate or bisoprolol served as controls. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality or all-cause hospitalization during the 3-year follow-up. Propensity score matching (PSM) balanced confounders. Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to estimate event-free survival, and hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated using Cox proportional hazards models for time-to-event outcomes. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate the robustness of the findings. RESULTS: Overall, 75 230 patients received carvedilol and 21 587 received metoprolol/bisoprolol. After PSM, 20 939 patients were included in each group. Carvedilol was associated with a higher risk of the primary composite endpoint compared with those taking metoprolol or bisoprolol (52.32% vs 46.29%; HR: 1.21; 95% CI, 1.17-1.24; P < .0001). Carvedilol was also linked to increased hospitalization risk (HR: 1.32; 95% CI, 1.28-1.36; P < .0001) but a modest reduction in mortality (HR: 0.92; 95% CI, 0.87-0.97; P = .0011). In addition, carvedilol was associated with higher risks of hypotension, end-stage renal disease, and bradycardia. Sensitivity analysis results were consistent for the primary endpoint. CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Our results suggest that carvedilol may be associated with a higher risk of the composite endpoint, health care utilization, and adverse events but lower all-cause mortality compared with metoprolol or bisoprolol in patients with HFrEF taking sacubitril/valsartan.

articles.title: Design, In Silico Targeting, and Characterization of Curcumin-Ibuprofen Prodrug Microspheres for Brain-Specific Delivery in Alzheimer's Therapy.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative condition characterized by limited treatment effectiveness, attributed to inadequate Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) permeability and low medication absorption. Curcumin and ibuprofen possess anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties but are limited by pharmacokinetic constraints. This study aimed to synthesize a curcumin-ibuprofen mutual prodrug (CIP), formulate it into chitosan-based microspheres (CIPM), and evaluate its neuroprotective potential for brain-targeted delivery in AD. METHODS: CIP was synthesized via ethylenediamine carbodiimide (EDCI) mediated esterification and confirmed through IR, NMR, LC-MS, and DSC. CIPM microspheres were prepared using emulsion crosslinking, characterized by scanning electron microscopy, drug entrapment efficiency (85.5%), zeta potential, particle size analysis, and DSC. In silico tools (SwissADME, ProTox-II) and molecular docking were used to assess ADMET profiles and target binding (AChE, BACE1, β-secretase). Network pharmacology identified overlapping targets between curcumin and AD. In vivo evaluation was conducted in a TMT (Trimethyltin)- induced neurodegeneration rat model through behavioral Morris Water Maze (MWM), Novel Object Recognition (NOR), Social Recognition Test (SRT), and biochemical and histological assessments. RESULTS: CIP demonstrated strong binding affinity with AD-related targets (-10.0 to -8.5 kcal/mol) and favorable ADMET properties. Network analysis identified 226 overlapping targets and key hub genes. CIPM significantly improved cognitive performance, antioxidant enzyme levels, and neuronal integrity compared to individual drugs and showed comparable efficacy to donepezil. DISCUSSION: The present study demonstrates that the curcumin-ibuprofen conjugate, when delivered through chitosan-based microspheres, effectively enhances brain targeting and overcomes pharmacokinetic barriers. The formulation not only improved drug bioavailability but also showed superior neuroprotective and cognitive benefits compared to individual drugs. Molecular docking and network pharmacology further confirmed its multi-target potential, suggesting a synergistic mechanism in modulating key AD pathways. These outcomes highlight CIPM as a promising candidate that warrants further pharmacokinetic and clinical validations for Alzheimer's therapy. CONCLUSION: The curcumin-ibuprofen prodrug-loaded microspheres present a promising brain-targeted treatment approach for Alzheimer's disease by improving bioavailability, engaging multiple targets, and providing neuroprotection.

articles.title: Decoding Pyroptosis in Pulmonary Fibrosis: Molecular Mechanisms and Therapeutic Horizons.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a progressive and fatal interstitial lung disease characterized by the depletion of alveolar epithelial cells (AECs) and the pathological accumulation of extracellular matrix (ECM). Despite its high mortality rate, the molecular drivers of PF progression remain partially understood. Recent evidence suggests that pyroptosis, a pro-inflammatory programmed cell death, plays a pivotal role in orchestrating the inflammatory cascade and fibrotic remodeling in the lung. METHODS: This study employed bibliometric and visual analysis via CiteSpace 6.2.4 to systematically map the research landscape of pyroptosis in PF using the Web of Science Core Collection (2010-2025). Based on the identified hotspots, a comprehensive review of the molecular activation pathways and cell-specific mechanisms was conducted. RESULTS: Bibliometric analysis (Modularity Q=0.5381, Silhouette S=0.8236) revealed a significant shift in research focus from basic pathological descriptions (2010-2015) to detailed pyroptotic mechanisms (2015- 2020), with immune checkpoint inhibitors emerging as the latest frontier since 2020. Mechanistically, we propose an "Initiation-Amplification-Persistence" model: AEC pyroptosis initiates epithelial barrier disruption; macrophage pyroptosis amplifies the inflammatory storm and polarizes the immune microenvironment; and fibroblast activation sustains ECM deposition. Furthermore, we summarized potential therapeutic interventions, including small molecule synthetic compounds (Nintedanib, Pirfenidone, MCC950, VX-765, etc.), natural products (Lycorine, Tanshinone IIA, etc.) and biologically active substances (Canakinumab, Anakinra) that exhibit multi-pathway synergistic effects. CONCLUSION: Targeting the pyroptosis signaling axis offers a promising strategy for reversing PF progression. Future research should prioritize the identification of pyroptosis- related biomarkers and the development of lung-targeted delivery systems to facilitate clinical translation and precision intervention.

articles.title: Correspondence Comments on "Differential effects of alcohol-derived serum metabolites and direct ethanol exposure on mouse preantral follicle development".
